label: Q-02
title: Phase 9.7's maxMintPerDay restore assertion is vacuous locally: the pre-value is 0, which is exactly what registerStablecoin resets to
fingerprintVerified: re-derived by finding-manager as sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass:entryPoint); matches verbatim
description: Story 089's Background names the trap this phase exists to rehearse: registerStablecoin resets maxMintPerDay to 0 (PhusdStableMinter.sol:125), so setMaxMintPerDay must be re-applied. Its acceptance criterion is 'maxMintPerDay equals its value before re-registration'. DeployMocks never sets a non-zero DOLA cap, so prevMaxMintPerDay == 0 (logged: 'maxMintPerDay restored: 0'). If the setMaxMintPerDay line (2521) were deleted, `require(maxMintPerDay == prevMaxMintPerDay)` would still pass.
impact: The rehearsal reports the reset-then-restore ordering as asserted while proving nothing about it. A future regression in that ordering would pass dev silently.
evidence: dev-run.filtered.log Phase 9.7 line 'maxMintPerDay restored: 0'; PhusdStableMinter.registerStablecoin writes maxMintPerDay: 0; grep shows no other setMaxMintPerDay for DOLA in DeployMocks.
attackPath: 1. DeployMocks never sets a non-zero DOLA cap, so prevMaxMintPerDay == 0.
3. The restore check compares 0 to 0 and cannot fail, so a future regression that drops the re-apply passes dev silently.

justification: QA. This is a vacuous post-condition on a local UI-mock script. The story-089 acceptance criterion is literally met (0 == 0), so it is not an F deviation, but the evidence for it carries no information. It has no asset or availability impact. It is kept as Q-02, and not set aside under the 2026-09-15 ruling, because it is a test-adequacy defect in dev's own assertion. Since the remedy touches local fidelity, the ruling question is left visible for the owner (humanReviewFlag).
recommendation: Seed a non-zero DOLA cap at registration (setMaxMintPerDay(DOLA, X)) and require prevMaxMintPerDay > 0 before the restore check as an anti-vacuity gate, matching Phase 11.7's pattern. If the owner rules this within the UI-mock ruling, triage it as wont-fix and cite the ruling.
